title: Bad Ideas Only
description: About the Opportunity Tired of trying to build the next unicorn startup? Good. Welcome to Bad Ideas Only , hosted by Hoollow. This is a satirical, 100% online pitch competition where your only goal is to invent the absolute worst, most over-engineered, and utterly useless tech product possible. We don't want real solutions; we want chaotic system architectures, terrible business models, and AI-generated mockups for a problem that doesn't exist. No manual coding is required. Bring your best prompt engineering skills, generate a hilarious pitch deck, and sell your terrible idea to our panel of "investors" with absolute, deadpan confidence.   Join Whatsapp Community:  https://chat.whatsapp.com/COlNXWGsUNi7fervSHTgrC   Stages and Timelines Round 1: The Pitch Deck Submission (Online) Brainstorm your useless tech product with your team. Generate your absurd business plan. Submit your idea as a presentation through the Unstop portal. Round 2: The "Shark Tank" Showdown (Live Pitch & Q&A) The Top 10 shortlisted teams from Round 1 will be invited to our live online stage (via Zoom/Google Meet). You will pitch your terrible startup live, followed by a hilarious and ruthless cross-questioning Q&A session from our panel and the live audience. Rule: You must maintain character and defend your chaotic tech stack as if it is a brilliant billion-dollar idea. The Final Result From the Top 10 live pitches, the judges will crown the Top 3 ultimate winners based on the absurdity of the architecture, the humor of the pitch, and the creative use of AI. title: CTF Cicada 2026
description: Overview CTF CICADA 2026 – Capture The Flag Organised by IEEE Student Branch & IET On Campus, BIT Mesra Get ready to enter the world of cryptic clues, hidden messages, ciphers, and challenging puzzles! CTF CICADA 2026 brings back our Capture The Flag competition with an entirely new experience inspired by Cicada 3301 , the mysterious internet puzzle phenomenon that captivated thousands of people worldwide. This year, we are moving beyond the traditional Jeopardy-style CTF format and introducing an Alternate Reality Game (ARG)-style experience . Participants will navigate through 30 levels, each presenting a trail of clues that must be deciphered to unlock the next stage. Whether you enjoy cryptography, cybersecurity, logical reasoning, digital investigation, or solving unconventional puzzles, CICADA is your opportunity to put your skills to the test. Event Format Competition: Capture The Flag (CTF) Format: ARG-style, fully online Total Levels: 30 Team Size: 1–3 members Participation: Open across India Duration: 10 December 2026 – 10 January 2027 What Makes CICADA Different? Unlike conventional CTF competitions that present standalone challenges on a leaderboard, CICADA follows a progressive puzzle-solving journey. 30 Progressive Levels: Every level contains a trail of clues. Solve one to unlock the next. ARG-Inspired Challenges: Explore clues involving images, ciphers, websites, and hidden information. Staged Releases: Levels will open in stages and remain accessible until the competition ends. Hints Along the Way: Hints will be released to help participants progress. No Elimination: Participants can continue solving challenges throughout the competition period. Who Can Participate? CICADA 2026 welcomes curious, analytical, and technically inclined participants from across India. You can participate: Individually, or In a team of 2–3 members. Bring your friends together, form a team, and take on the challenge. Prizes and Recognition Exciting prizes for the winning teams. E-certificates for every participant. Recognition for outstanding performance. About the Organisers IEEE Student Branch and IET On Campus at Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra, Ranchi, are student-run campus chapters of two leading engineering societies. Since 2019, we have been organising Capture The Flag competitions, technical events, and hands-on workshops covering Linux, Git, Python, web development, and more. With CICADA 2026, we aim to bring an engaging, month-long puzzle-solving experience to participants across India. Important Dates Competition Starts: 10 December 2026 Competition Ends: 10 January 2027 Mode: Completely Online Get ready to decode, investigate, collaborate, and uncover what lies beyond the next clue. Organised by: IEEE Student Branch & IET On Campus Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra, Ranchi The trail is waiting. Will you follow it? CTF CICADA 2026 – Every clue leads somewhere.

title: ELU Build
description: About ELUBuild ELUBuild is the flagship solo product-building challenge by EduLinkUp . Over the course of the buildathon, individual builders pitch innovative software ideas, and once approved, build, document, and ship real-world SaaS applications from the ground up. The mission of ELUBuild is to discover and empower solo builders to create sustainable, user-ready digital products. Exceptional projects will be selected for integration into the ELU Store platform, with opportunities for direct deployment, hosting, and potential publishing on the Google Play Store on behalf of EduLinkUp. The Complete Event Flow ELUBuild runs across clear, structured phases: Registration & Track Exploration: Register via the EduLinkUp mobile app. Review the announced tracks and loose problem statement suggestions provided by EduLinkUp. These serve as inspiration-participants are completely free to think beyond these suggestions and tackle any authentic, high-impact problem within the domain. Use this phase to brainstorm, validate needs, and prepare your pitch before the idea portal opens. Idea Submission Phase: When the idea window opens, submit your idea proposal (project name, problem statement, target users, proposed solution, anticipated tech stack, solo buildability feasibility, and an explanatory video link). You can submit anytime while the window is active. Continuous Review & Approval: The EduLinkUp team reviews submissions on a rolling basis. Ideas can be approved at any time while the window is open. Share Your Vision: Once your idea is approved, you can (and are encouraged to) publish your explanatory pitch video on social media. Social Media Engagement Leaderboard (Active in Idea & Build Phases): A dedicated engagement leaderboard tracks reach, quality, and engagement of participants' social media posts across both the Idea Phase and the Building Phase . Compelling explanations, progress updates, and demos that resonate with the community rank higher. Idea Phase Closure, Review & Stage 1 Certification: The idea submission portal closes at 11:59 PM IST on the deadline day. The final review round is completed, and results are officially released to all participants. Stage 1 Certification: All builders whose ideas are approved receive official Stage 1 ELUBuild recognition and advance to the building phase. Building Phase (Next.js + Supabase): Building takes place inside the edulinkup-interns GitHub organisation. Shortlisted builders create their public repository under edulinkup-interns . Mandatory Tech Stack: Projects must be built using Next.js and Supabase , with authentication integrated via EduLinkUp OAuth ( @edulinkup/auth SDK). Detailed step by step instructions/guide of connecting your site with EduLinkUp OAuth will be shared before the building phase. Weekly Social Updates: Builders must share at least one weekly progress update on social media (e.g., #buildinpublic , feature demos, architecture highlights, or lessons learned). Engaging, authentic content helps you climb the Social Leaderboard. Repository Commits & Commit Quality Leaderboard: Steady, consistent development through the build window is tracked on a dedicated Commit Leaderboard . Quality & Consistency Over Raw Volume: Scoring evaluates steady engineering rhythm, meaningful commit messages, and genuine code evolution-not artificial commit spamming or scripts. Manual Audits: Code and repository activity will be regularly inspected manually. Use of commit bots, artificial commit scripts, or bulk dumping pre-existing code on the final day will lead to immediate disqualification . Final Submission & Judging: Submit your GitHub repository (under edulinkup-interns ), a deployed live demo URL, and a comprehensive product walkthrough video. Independent evaluations determine top ranks (Winner / Top 1, Top 3, Top 5, Top 7, and All participants). Event Conclusion, Rewards & ELU Store Integration: Winners and top builders receive trophies, official swags kits, domain vouchers, AI interview vouchers, and certificates. ELU Store Launch: The best app(s) are selected for ecosystem integration into the ELU Store , with maintenance support, live showcase, and potential Google Play Store publication under the EduLinkUp organisation. Participation & Eligibility Solo Builders Only: Participation is strictly individual. No teams, shared accounts, or outsourced engineering. App-Verified Registration: Registration must be completed via the official EduLinkUp Android app. GitHub Requirement: A valid GitHub profile link must be provided. EduLinkUp issues invitations to the edulinkup-interns organization. Ensure you accept the GitHub organization invite before the build window starts. One Idea Per Participant: Each builder may submit one proposal per edition. Ideas can be edited until the submission window closes. Idea Proposal Submission Guidelines Your pitch must address a real-world problem and clearly articulate how it will be delivered solo. Submissions include: Project Name: Clear, brandable name for your product. Problem Statement: Specific, concrete friction point you are solving. Target Users: Exact demographic or professional segment that experiences this problem. Evidence of Need: Why this problem exists and proof that users care. Proposed Solution: Your functional approach and feature roadmap. Anticipated Tech Stack: Confirmation of Next.js, Supabase, and auxiliary APIs/libraries. Solo Buildability Note: Feasibility explanation detailing how the core MVP can be built solo within the build window. Idea Video Link: A public link (YouTube, Loom, Google Drive) explaining your concept clearly in English or Hindi (1-3 minutes). Note: Ideas are reviewed on merit and feasibility. Clearing this stage qualifies you for the Stage 1 Certificate and unlocks the Building Phase. Technical & Building Standards All projects in the building phase must adhere to the following rules: GitHub Organization: All code must live inside a public repository created in the edulinkup-interns GitHub organisation. Repository ownership remains with the organisation. Standard Tech Stack: Frontend & Framework: Next.js (App Router recommended). Backend & Database: Individual Supabase project owned and managed by the participant. Authentication: EduLinkUp OAuth using @edulinkup/auth . Detailed step-by-step instructions and guides for connecting your application with EduLinkUp OAuth will be shared with all shortlisted builders prior to the building phase. Genuine Work Created in Window: All code must be authored during the active build window. Re-submitting existing projects or templates with trivial tweaks is strictly prohibited. Secret Security: Never commit service-role keys, private API secrets, or database passwords to public repositories. Utilise .env.local and environment variables. Permitted Resources: Open-source npm packages, public APIs, and AI coding assistants (e.g., Gemini, Copilot, Cursor) are allowed, provided you understand, customize, and own your codebase. Integrity & Anti-Bot Rule: Commits must reflect authentic engineering progress. Scripted commit bots, fake green-square generators, or plagiarized repos result in immediate disqualification. Final Submission Checklist At the conclusion of the build window, participants submit: Repository Link: Working, clean repository in edulinkup-interns . Live Production URL: A fast, functional deployed application (e.g., on Vercel) that judges and visitors can test directly. Demo & Walkthrough Video: Public video demonstrating the end-to-end user workflow, core features, and product value. Builder Philosophy ELUBuild is not an academic exercise or a mock hackathon. It is a launchpad to build an authentic, lasting software product that people genuinely use. Build independently. Build publicly. Build something worth keeping. A solo product-building competition: pitch an idea, and if it is shortlisted, build and ship it in the build window. Each edition has one fixed track and one winner.

title: Rabinjathon: Prime 1
description: Overview RABINJATHON is a student-led, online-first innovation and project-building event organized by RABINJA SQUAD. The event is designed for participants who want to take an idea beyond a presentation — develop a concept, build a working prototype or demonstrable solution, explain how it works, and present it before a panel of judges. The event will begin in an online format. Depending on the event schedule and feasibility, selected/final-stage activities may be conducted in a hybrid format. Any confirmed hybrid requirements, venue details, or physical participation information will be communicated to eligible participants in advance. Event Approach Participants are expected to develop their own original idea, product, prototype, or solution. There is no single fixed problem statement that every team must solve. Participants may work across different areas such as software, web development, hardware, robotics, open innovation, and other technology-oriented concepts. The focus is on creativity, development, demonstration, communication, and practical thinking. Participants are encouraged to build and demonstrate a functional prototype wherever reasonably possible. Teams should be able to explain what their solution does, how it works, and what problem it is intended to address. Eligibility & Team Format Participation is open to students and eligible learners as specified in the registration requirements. Solo participation is allowed. Teams may consist of 1–4 participants. Inter-college teams are allowed. Participants from different academic specializations/branches may form a team. Team members do not need to belong to the same college, course, or specialization. Each participant should provide accurate information during registration. Participants may be required to provide additional details or proof of eligibility if requested by the organizers. A team can therefore be formed around the idea and skills required for the project rather than being restricted to one institution or specialization. Event Format RABINJATHON: PRIME 1 will progress through multiple stages. The rounds are designed to evaluate not only the idea itself, but also how participants develop, demonstrate, communicate, and defend their solution. Round 1 — Product Introduction / Ad-Style Video Participants will create a short video of approximately 2 minutes introducing their product, project, or solution. The video should be presented in an engaging, attention-grabbing format similar to a professional product advertisement or launch introduction. The video should communicate: Product/project name Product logo or visual identity, where applicable The problem or need being addressed A concise introduction to the solution Key value or purpose of the product Why someone would be interested in the solution An engaging introduction that captures the viewer's attention Participants may use creative storytelling, demonstrations, visuals, mock advertisements, animations, or other suitable presentation techniques. Where a participant uses an officially sponsored/partnered product, service, API, platform, or tool, the relevant sponsor/partner branding may be required to be displayed or acknowledged according to the applicable usage guidelines and permissions. Participants must not imply sponsorship, endorsement, partnership, or affiliation with any company unless such relationship has been officially confirmed and authorized. Detailed Round 1 submission instructions, technical requirements, submission procedure, deadlines, and any applicable branding requirements will be shared with registered participants approximately one week before the round. Round 2 — Project Showcase / Working Explainer Participants progressing to Round 2 will create a video of up to 5 minutes explaining their project in greater depth. This round is intended to demonstrate that the concept is not only an idea, but something that has been developed, prototyped, tested, or otherwise demonstrated to a meaningful extent. Participants should explain: What the project does The problem being addressed How the solution works Major components or technologies involved The current stage of development Prototype/demo functionality How the product could work in a real-world scenario What makes the approach different or useful Think of this round as a behind-the-scenes product showcase — similar to how technology and manufacturing programmes demonstrate a product being developed and prepared, while keeping confidential implementation details or proprietary "secret sauce" private. Participants are NOT required to publicly disclose sensitive intellectual property, confidential algorithms, private credentials, proprietary datasets, or other information they do not wish to reveal. The objective is to provide enough evidence and demonstration to establish that the project has been meaningfully developed. Final Round — Live Pitch & Judge Interaction Finalists will present their ideas/projects before a panel of judges. The final presentation will allow participants to: Present the problem and proposed solution Demonstrate or explain the developed product/prototype Explain the project's working and implementation Discuss practical applications and future possibilities Answer questions from the judging panel Respond to feedback and observations from the judges Judges may ask questions regarding the idea, implementation, technology, feasibility, originality, demonstration, or potential application of the project. Following the interaction, the judging panel will evaluate the submissions according to the applicable judging criteria and may provide suggestions, observations, or feedback to the participants. Timeline Registration Opens: 18 October 2026 Registration Deadline: As specified on the official Unstop opportunity page. Round 1: Scheduled after the registration phase. Detailed submission instructions and the confirmed Round 1 timeline will be communicated to registered participants approximately one week before the round. Round 2: Participants qualifying from Round 1 will receive the Round 2 submission schedule and instructions in advance. Final Round: Finalists will receive the final presentation schedule, format, and participation instructions in advance. Event Mode: Online-first. Hybrid Component: A hybrid component may be introduced for selected/final-stage activities depending on the finalized event plan and feasibility. Any confirmed physical participation requirements will be communicated separately in advance. Participants should regularly check the official Unstop opportunity page and the communication channels provided by the organizers for schedule updates. General Rules Participants must submit their own work and provide accurate information during registration. Plagiarism, fraudulent submissions, impersonation, fabricated results, or misrepresentation of a project's development status may result in disqualification. Teams must have 1–4 members and should ensure that all registered team members are genuine participants. Participants may use publicly available technologies, frameworks, APIs, development tools, AI-assisted tools, libraries, and other legitimate resources unless specifically restricted in the round instructions. If external tools, APIs, datasets, models, or third-party resources are used, participants should disclose their meaningful use where requested by the organizers or judging criteria. Participants must not share passwords, API keys, private credentials, confidential information, or other sensitive data in their submissions. Participants must respect the intellectual property rights, licenses, trademarks, and usage conditions of third-party software, APIs, datasets, media, logos, and other resources. Company, sponsor, partner, or product logos must not be used in a way that falsely suggests endorsement, sponsorship, or official partnership. Any confirmed sponsor/partner branding requirements communicated by the organizers must be followed. Participants are responsible for ensuring that submitted videos, images, music, software, datasets, and other materials can legally be used in their submission. Participants should not disclose confidential or proprietary information that they are not authorized to share. The organizers may request clarification, supporting material, a demonstration, or additional information regarding a submission where necessary for evaluation. Participants must follow the submission format, file requirements, deadlines, and other instructions communicated for each round. Late or incomplete submissions may not be considered unless an exception is explicitly communicated by the organizers. The organizers reserve the right to disqualify submissions that violate the event rules or applicable laws. The judging panel's evaluation will be based on the criteria communicated for the respective stage. Any event updates, schedule changes, additional requirements, or round-specific instructions will be communicated through the official channels used for the event. Important RABINJATHON is organized as a student-led initiative by RABINJA SQUAD. The event is intended to provide participants with an opportunity to build, showcase, communicate, and receive feedback on their ideas and projects. Participants should not assume that participation, selection, judging feedback, sponsorship, partnership, publication, investment, employment, or any other external opportunity is guaranteed unless it is explicitly confirmed by the organizers. Specific round instructions, judging criteria, submission requirements, branding requirements, and timelines may be updated or communicated separately as the event progresses. Participants are encouraged to keep checking the official event page and organizer communications for the latest information. Participants can join the official WhatsApp group for event-related communication and updates: WhatsApp Group Participants are encouraged to keep checking the official event page and organizer communications for the latest information.

description: Complete Regsiteration and Submission at: https://techfest.org/competitions/Algo It is mandatory to register on Techfest Website . further details will be updated on the Website only . About The Algo Trading Innovation Challenge is a national fintech competition by Delta Exchange and Techfest, IIT Bombay, built around a stark fact: SEBI found that 87.7% of individual equity-derivatives traders made net losses in FY26. Teams study Delta Exchange's AlgoHub, its ecosystem of six algorithmic trading features, identify a significant gap that Futures and Options traders face, and design an original, AI-assisted capability that goes beyond what the platform offers today. The top 50 teams turn their ideas into working prototypes at an on-campus hackathon at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia's largest science and technology festival. Structure The competition runs in two rounds, with Round 2 as an on-campus hackathon at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Eligibility: Open to all students with a valid ID from their educational institution. Cross-institutional teams are encouraged. Team size: Maximum 4 members per team. The Challenge: Teams select one or two (maximum two) of the six AlgoHub features, Algo Marketplace, Algo Builder, API Copilot, Trading Bot, APIs, or Trade Data, identify a significant product gap or unmet need that F&O traders face within them, and design an innovative, AI-assisted capability that adds meaningful functionality beyond what exists today. Teams may propose an independent innovation per feature or one unified solution covering both. Delta Exchange is already working on natural-language strategy creation, backtesting, and trading intelligence, so teams are encouraged not to build their proposal primarily around those capabilities. Round 1 - Online Submission (Screening) A conceptual round; no working prototype is required and teams do not need to deploy live strategies or trade with real capital. Teams submit a presentation of no more than 6 slides (PPT/PPTX or PDF export) covering: Selected Feature(s) & Product Understanding Problem Identification & Product Gap Proposed AI-Assisted Innovation Real-World Trading Use Case Technical Approach & Feasibility Expected Impact & Value Only the Team Leader may submit. The 50 highest-scoring teams qualify for Round 2; ties at the cutoff are broken by the higher score in Innovation & AI Application, then Problem Identification & Trader Relevance, then Technical Feasibility. Round 2 - On-Campus Hackathon at IIT Bombay The top 50 teams develop their proposed innovations into working prototypes and demonstrate them at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Detailed format and judging guidelines will be shared with shortlisted teams. Timeline Registration closes - 30th November 2026 Round 1 submission deadline - 30th November 2026 Shortlist announcement - 5th December 2026 Finals (on-campus hackathon at IIT Bombay) - 15th-18th December 2026 Rewards and Prizes INR 50,000 for the top 3 winners. Certificates for all participants who qualify for Round 2.
